It’s my first to move-in day volunteer. Different from my expectation, it’s to assist first-year students with moving luggage. So tired. Between 9 am to 1 pm, I helped 10+ family to move their luggage. All of them took tons of luggage. I am not exaggerating, literally, mountain piles. But totally understood, first time to leave from home and start a new chapter, which reminded me my first day entering to this campus. I received thanks from them, and felt their happiness and looking forward to the future. It seems every student felt they are lucky to get exactly the room they want, some lived in high floor with good view, some lived close to emergency exit. I met different families from different backgrounds. One is Canadian family from Calgary, a mother and her daughter. To my surprise, they didn’t went to Moraine Lake yet, that’s a bit pity. One is very complex: father is Chinese, mother is Korean and met in France. I heard they communicated with four languages, Eng, French, Korean, Mandarin. One girl is from India, with parents and elder brother. They had the least luggage, simple but sufficient. (Biaoyang) They are kind. TBH, I was a bit biased before, but I met many friendly Indians, who are willing to help you. The girl told me she wanted to major in microbiology and immunology. (respect!) Overall, I felt it’s worth being volunteer. And happy to meet new people. I added another volunteer’s Ins, who majors in psychology cuz I wanted to persuade her to try and take Psyc 309 together next term lol.

I recently went to Hong Kong to visit two friends, one of whom was my college roommate. The last time we saw each other was at our undergrad graduation last year, so it had been a while. Moving forward, meeting up with certain people—including family and friends—is going to become fewer and far between. In the end, I went to the beach with a friend I met during my internship. Hanging out by the sea really melts the stress away.
In an in-person training session for an event, there were around 70-ish participants, and everyone had a chance to win a hoodie by lottery. I was the only one selected.
My landlord handed me some tomatoes that they planted and grew. I used them to make delicious food. We also had a short conversation regarding my recent experience and future plan.

I spent a long time doing perler-bead crafts today. I kept miscounting the grids and my hands shook constantly. My eyes and back started to ache, yet I still felt a little proud of what I was making. x

Yesterday I met a former colleague for breakfast. She is the most chaotic person I have ever known. It's always an adventure! I sat there sipping my coffee as the text came through telling me she was running late. I expected that even though she had initially told me our meeting could only last 46 minutes as she had another commitment afterwards. Then came the next text. She was late because her pregnant daughter was en route home from India when her flight was detained due to issues with flights over Pakistan. It's never a little issue with her, God lover her. Once she arrived we had a lovely meal before she scurried off, now late for her next meeting.

nothing dramatic just a screwed up day. i was anxious most of the day and felt out of it. i went with my car to do an errand and ended up driving aimlessly in a rural area near my home. i stopped at a restaurant and ate which helped calm me. I went home, did some minor housework and distracted my self by watching TV. I hoped for better times.

Yesterday my youngest son needed to see a doctor. He has been having ear pain and woke up Monday to find that one of his ears was bleeding inside. That afternoon I tried to get an appointment in an urgent care facility but after waiting over two hours I was told they had an emergency and couldn’t see him that day. So I tried again yesterday, but to no avail. The clinic was full again and another location that they referred us to was overbooked. So, as a last resort, I called the pediatrician (who I thought wouldn’t be able to fit us in at the last minute). He had an opening for a “virtual “ appointment. It only took about 5 minutes and we didn’t even have to leave the house!

Nothing particularly interesting happened yesterday. It was a typical day. It snowed for most of the day so I didn't take my daily walk. Instead I spent much of the day reading and writing. I started a new book called The Last Bookshop in London. It's a work of historical fiction that deals with London just before and during WWII. The main character has just moved to London from the English countryside and takes a job as an assistant in a book store. She isn't a book person and knows absolutely nothing about books. I love history and my favorite genre to read is historical fiction. I can't imagine someone who doesn't read books, but that's one of the things that makes this book so interesting. I assume there will be a love interest coming along too. I also spent a good bit of the day writing. I am a children's writer and am in the midst of a freelance writing project. I also listened to a zoom meeting about writing in the evening. After that I sat down with my husband to watch a little TV. I crocheted while watching.

Yesterday was just another Covid 19 social isolation day. Suuny, and pleasant, although not super warm here in the Chicago area. Lots of people out and about, taking the kids for a walk and going for runs with the puppies, etc... Our house is filled with sunlight when the sun is out, so that really cheers me up alot. I watched the morning news, had my coffee, took a shower, because my hair was all glued together! I m trying to be more like my usual self and pay better attention to my grooming, as I usually do, as this pandemic has made me a little cavalier about that! I figure my husband has to look at me, so I should try to look a bit nicer ..even if I'm not going out, so I do make the effort...most days! I went downstiars after fixing myself up, and my husband was working out, so I got started on my workout,.. We are both 69, and my husband has numberous serious health problems, walks and does calisthenics.I will say here, that we only go out once a week or so, as covid 19 would be lethal for my husband with his conditions, and who knows how bad any of us will get it? Answer..we dbn't. ..I am in much better health, so I do more rigorous workouts. SO, I worked out to a new You Tube video my husband found for me...hes so helpful, lol. It was exhausting, but I made it through! Also got my 10k steps in on my Fitbit...My husband took a nap and I read the paper and did a few other things. We made salad and tv dinners , not our usual sunday faire, but this is a pandemic situation, as I keep telling my husband! I had planned to do a bunch of things yesterday, like paying business bills, and personal bills, drawing, etc..but somehow the day got away from me. That will happen when you are stuck at home almost 24/7!! I m determined to be more productive today..Its another beautiful day out.

Yesterday was basically just like any other day. I did my usual laundry, housework and took care of our 5 cats. My Husband was working out in the garage and decided to get my bicycle out of the back of the garage, where it had been stored for a few years. He cleaned it up and inflated the tires. I spent a lot of the day, between housework, going outside, in the warm summer weather, and riding my bike. At the end of the day, I took my bicycle into the house and found a place to store it, so that I could get to it easily.

I woke up earlier than usual yesterday and was thinking about the current pandemic. I lay in bed wishing the world would go back to "normal," for a few minutes and then got up and started my day. I sat down at my desk and looked at work that I needed to complete for the day. I then logged into my school site to check assignments, because I am in graduate school for a Masters degree in English and my latest class started this week. I wrote my introduction post to share with my peers. I logged out and after that I worked for several hours on editing tasks and other data entry that I needed to get finished. I had a sandwich for lunch and decided to take a short nap. I slept for an hour and a half, longer than I wanted to, but that was probably because I woke up early. I went back to work in the afternoon and took a few breaks to have conversations with my adult son who lives with me with his wife and young daughter. In the evening, I decided to relax a bit and play a video game because that is relaxing to me. I did a bit more work after that and answered an email from a friend. I went to bed fairly early and read a book until I fell asleep.

Yesterday, I decided to go out for a walk after I got the mail. I put on my face mask and went out. In the distance I saw an oder woman walking ahead of me. I had seen her before. She always wears a face mask because of the pandemic. She walks a few steps and looks around. Then she walks a bit mre and looks around. As I got close to her, I moved to the grass to the right. I also called out a "Hello" to not scare her. She stopped and looked at me. I stopped too and said "Hello" again. She said "Hello" and said that these days people were afraid to talk to each other. I was the first stranger who had greeted her in ages. I agreed tthat people were afraid of each other. I asked if she'd like to walk together but spaced out. She agreed. We walked and talked. I learned her name and that she lives in the next building. She has kids and grandkids but while they call eac other on the phone, they don;t get together for visits yet. She said they're afraid of giving her the virus by accident. So we had a nice chat and walk. We plan to do it again. Yesterday evening I was sitting on my third-floor balcony and saw her walking by again. I called out tp her and she looked up. She seemed happy to see me and we had a short chat. Then she walked off again. People need people even if we do have to wear face masks.

Yesterday, I had a phone conversation with a client who discussed a new business deal with me. She needed me to do some work for her company on a contractual basis. We talked about what she needed, how I could help and all the details that go into such things. It was a pleasant conversation. I had done business with her before and I didn’t need to “hard sell” her on my services or abilities. It was a good conversation and yesterday’s discussion ended with me having to send her a proposal to sign and she had to email me more details about exactly what she wanted me to do.

Yesterday I was invited to a Zoom reunion with the debate coach at my high school, now in his eighties (I'm in my sixties!). I heard about it through my brother, a friend of his having been on the team with me back then, and I was immediately excited to tell another friend of mine who had particularly loved this coach. She and I had not spoken for a decade, and the last time we did, it had been difficult. She more or less withdrew from me at that time, disappointed in my religious affiliation and too busy for me. I had missed her and thought this might be a good time to reconnect. It took me a long time to track her down, then the Google trail got cold, and I ended up calling her ex-husband, whose number I did find, only to be told by his (new) wife that my friend had died of cancer five years ago. I hadn't known.

Yesterday was a deja vu day because of the Coronavirus. My husband and I are in our 70's and living in the country in New Mexico. It is beautiful with the view of the mountains and mostly sunny days. We are lucky to be retired because it must be so hard for those who lost their jobs due to the virus. For activities, yesterday I watched, for Holocaust Remembrance Day, four films about the holocaust which, unfortunately, hits home and is depressing. I also read a Kindle book about Larry Nassar who was sexually abusing young gymnasts some years ago. I love my iPad and so I played word games and casual games on it. I didn't exercise yesterday, but I plan to today. I guess I'm very appreciative of life since a few years back I recovered from a stroke, and recently recovered from breast cancer. I talked to my daughters on the phone and on Facetime. We have three cats and in the evening, they come into the house to watch movies with us. It will be similar every day as long as we need to stay home.

There aren't many personal life events for me lately. Because of the pandemic, I feel so isolated. To pass the time, I take surveys to escape the anxiety I'm faced with about the virus. I also cook for sustenance but also as a way of escaping the depression. Yesterday, my husband wanted me to cook black bean tostadas for dinner. I had to make a trip to the grocery store. Even though I feel uneasy going out and about, it also makes me feel somewhat normal and makes me think of a simpler, happier time. I made us a rather tasty dinner and made my husband very happy. I try to think of the positive things, and I'm thankful that I have my husband to keep me going at a time when I would otherwise do hardly anything. You see...everyday feels like groundhog day.

Yesterday I was doing laundry on a beautiful autumn day. As it dried, I took the opportunity to go scatter wild bird food across the side yard. The seed is a bountiful mixture that attracts different species of birds, squirrels, even some turkey and deer. Later that afternoon, I looked out the kitchen window to see a buck and doe stop and graze in the yard before they passed through the woods to settle in before dark.

I was talking with a business partner yesterday when the subject of politics came up. We have discussed politics in the past and have agreed on a variety of political issues in the past year, but something yesterday changed with their view and my view of the way things should be handled. Before February 2020 we had different views and could discuss them without too much anger coming up, but yesterday was a little different. We were discussing some of the executive orders that President Biden has signed and disagreed on a lot of them. We started having a heated argument about immigration, the military, and environmental issues. I am a Republican, and she is a Democrat so the two opposite parties usually clash on issues. But in the past year we have found some common ground and have had some good discussions. Yesterday was not one of those days, it was a major clash between us. Our voices were raised a few times as we tried to get our points across, and neither wanted to budge on their views. We probably had this conversation for a good hour or more, before we realized we were getting no where with the other person. I felt she was not being open minded, and I am sure she felt the same way about me. We decided to end the discussion abruptly before one of us said the wrong thing to the other and damage our business relationship. What was once a subject we could discuss freely was no more. I decided I would limit my discussion about politics in the future and respect her views but at the same time keep my principles. I do not want to see our business and personal relationship damaged over politics after having a working relationship for over 20 years.

Honestly, life right now can be pretty boring. The pandemic has ground almost everything to a stop and I rarely leave the house. But you are in luck, because yesterday something very exciting did happen...I received my first Covid vaccine. I am older, yes, but I qualified due to some underlying health conditions and was able to schedule an appointment through one of the hospitals near where I live. I didn't post anything about it on Facebook, but it was definitely an exciting event for me. My arm is sore today, but it was all worth it. I go back in 3 weeks to get the booster. I know that there are many people who do not want to take the vaccine. I am not one of them. I am and always have been in favor of vaccines for protection and this one is not different. I feel like I am doing my part to try to bring this pandemic to a close.

Yesterday was a rather difficult day for me. I work part time at an independent pet store. My boss, the owner of the store, had left the day before on a vacation and left me pretty much in charge. We were expecting 2 shipments to come in, which meant that once the order arrived we had to look up the prices in the computer (old school - no POS system) and then price the items and put them on the shelves. My work cohort and I had a plan in motion. I would look up the items, she would price them and we would each put them on the shelves. The first order didn't arrive until after 1 o'clock so we knew we had to rush to get this order put away before the 2nd order arrived. We finally got that accomplished and both sat down to take a break before the next order arrived. Until then, we also had to wait on customers. Now it is after 3 o'clock and there still is no 2nd order. We decide to call the distributor and ask where the truck is and are told that no order was placed. No order placed!!!! Of course right then a customer walks in which is probably good because we were both quite upset. It gave us time to calm down. My co worker came in early and I was staying late to accommodate the 2nd order. Once the customer left, I called my boss (thank God he was reachable by phone) who said that he didn't place a 2nd order and that he thought he had told us. No he hadn't told us. Anyway, I finished what work I had to do and went home. Exhausted!!! Thank God my partner was home and made dinner. I then got on the computer to see if there were any HITS in MTurk, and then off to bed.

Yesterday was a great day in our family. My sister is a first responder, and has logged in a ton of hours working as a nurse during this Pandemic. Although exercising every precaution, she was diagnosed positive on June 1. By the 4th, she was hospitalized, and soon was in the ICU. One of the symptoms of this virus is the development of blood clots in the lungs, and my sister had three of them. They gave her blood thinners, other medications , as well as the experimental drug Remdisivir. She began to respond well and by the 12th was out of the ICU, and in a regular room, she nicknamed 'the pod' because she was all isolated. She kept improving day by day, and yesterday, she went home. She is my best friend, and I felt so lucky to have her kick this virus' posterior. I cannot wait to see her, although it will be awhile. I have not seen her since this all began in March.

Yesterday was a day off from work, so I spent the day catching up on things I don't get to do on work days, like clean both bathrooms thoroughly. I also mopped my kitchen floor and caught up on my laundry. In the afternoon I had an appointment to get a mammogram, which I went to and felt good about because sometimes I am lax about getting one. After that I came home and started dinner and made a poppy seed cake for dessert. In between all this I snuck in a few chapters of a John LeCarre book I am reading. I had previously read most of this work but somehow missed reading The Little Drummer Girl. It's really good and I am enjoying it quite a bit. After dinner my husband and I went for a walk around the neighborhood. We have both put on unwanted pounds over the winter so we want to get back into a walking routine. Once we were home and the dishwasher loaded, my husband watched some TV and I read. At one point I spent some time speaking to our eldest daughter on the phone. I speak to her about every other day, but our youngest daughter only about once a week, she being busy with a job and two small boys. After the phone call I got ready for bed and then read another chapter or two before falling asleep. Not a terribly exciting day but one in which I caught up on cleaning and keeping an appointment, and then relaxing and puttering.

Yesterday, I imagined what it would be like if people did not suffer with allergies colds, pneumonia, bronchitis and all things related to these illnesses. What it would be like if we weren't coughing, sneezing, gasping for air, wheezing, taking medications and losing sleep. What if we didn't have to feel so miserable? One of my kids came down with bronchitis and I also succumbed to this illness. This has taken two good weeks out of our lives. Instead, we could have been blowing bubbles outside, baking Easter cookies and candy, coloring and doing things all kids love to do. Just for a time, I imagined how it would be not to suffer.

I went to go work out and got some groceries and when I got home I got a surprise in the mail and received a $27 check which was unexpected and I also got a package from my best Friend and also got a card from her with $20 in it as well, which was nice too.

It's Valentines Day. My wife and I have planned a celebration, not because of a phony capitalistic holiday made up to sell greeting cards, flowers and candy, but because we'd just closed the sale on our home up north. I left her at home briefly, somewhat to her dismay, while I ran out for a couple of fake errands I needed in order to accomplish my surprise. At the florist I opted to eschew the traditional roses for a bouquet of bright yellow and red tulips, a taste of spring in the midst of a long bitterly cold winter. It worked. She knew my opinion of Valentines Day so the surprise was a success that brought an appreciative welling to her eyes.

My life is boring these days. Yesterday I had a conversation with a neighbor about the things he and his wife are doing to fix up their home they just purchased. The weather this year was hard on all of us and some homes took it kind of poorly. They have a beautiful home but their brick fence fell down though not a surprise. They knew it needed repair. Now they are getting needed repairs made and figuring out how to fix the yard where the fence fell down. They are great neighbors and will get things fixed up.

We had some friends over for the weekend. For some reason we had played bridge until 12:20AM. I routinely get up at 5:30AM, so without even setting the alarm I was wide awake. The husband also woke up early and decided he wanted to make omelets. Sadly, we didn't have a pan that was like any that he uses at home, so it became a huge production number. After a couple of hours, everyone was up and about and had been feed some imperfect omelets. We mainly packed them out to their car to send them off, by noon they were on their way. However, I was pretty wrecked. I took a nap before our daily walk, and barely make the two mile walk. I dragged myself through the remainder of the day, mainly watching television. During the Voice, I fell asleep in my chair and a loud commercial woke me up. I gave up and went to bed at about 9:30PM, which caused me to wake up about three times during the night.

Yesterday I started on one of my New Year's resolutions for 2021. January 26, 2021--that's not so bad. Still January. I decided to embrace the Mediterranean Diet. Not a "diet" to lose weight, but rather a diet being the compilation of what a person eats. First I ordered a new cookbook, The Complete Mediterranean Cookbook by America's Test Kitchen. Then I chose some recipes in which I was interested. Next came the grocery store dilemma. The COVID-19 pandemic has made it an entirely different ballgame to go to the grocery store. My mom is 84yo and has several risk factors; I am 60yo with a few risk factors of my own. We strictly socially distance to avoid infection. I learned to use an app called InstaCart. It was weird to grocery shop from home. It actually took a long time to find everything. However, the city in which I live had just been gifted with 7 inches of snow in 24 hours. It was super nice to not have to slog to the store. My groceries were dropped off within 2 hours, and I started a recipe with ingredients that I had never cooked before: fennel bulbs and herbs de provence. I ended up making Spice-Rubbed Pork Tenderloin with Fennel, Tomatoes, Artichokes and Olives. I had also made Polenta with Parmesan Cheese and I had never even seen cornmeal before. The food turned out really delicious, and I am on my way to healthier eating!

Taking your 2006 car to get minor fixes done at the specialist garage is usually nothing but routine. “While you check the tire can you double check the CHECK ENGINE LIGHT, please? It came on while we drove over”. Oh. Oh no. The light alerted the garage that a major ($4000 !) problem was in the making. The lovely 2006 BMW530 wagon with 81,000 miles is being donated.

I have my 12 year old grandson spending some time with me. I bought him the game Pandemic since we are currently living in a real pandemic. I told him that his school work for the day was to figure out how to play the game and then teach me to play. I knew that this game was not an easy game to set-up and learn. I told him to read the instructions and use youtube videos to help. He spent almost 2 hours on this project while I did other things around the house. He was able to get the game set-up and figure out much of it but still could not completely understand the play of the game. I encouraged him to keep trying and repeatedly told him that I knew he could do it. Finally, as he became increasingly more frustrated I told him that when that happens to me that I leave it and come back to it later. I then told him that together we would figure out the rest of the game play tomorrow. I enjoyed seeing him use his brain to problem solve. Earlier in the day my grandson and I went to pick strawberries. I could see that it was a struggle for him to focus on the task but nevertheless we did get quite a supply in less than an hour. On our way home we stopped at Lowes to spend some time in the outside garden area. The majority of the people there were wearing masks and obviously trying to stay their distance. I found this to be distressing and overall did not find that trip very enjoyable at all. I wondered in my mind how long this new normal would go on.

I have just recently after a few decades away became a full-time college student. This happened as due to the pandemic I'm able to take the courses online, which for me is great. I am taking 12 units and yesterday an "event" would be just that I am now devoting hours during the day to working on one or two classes per day, in order to complete them. I consider every day that I'm studying a positive event.

Not many things happen these days since we are in the time of Covid. So events are small, but that doesn't make them insignificant. I woke up at dawn for the normal routine of feeding Molly and taking her out for her morning walk. I looked up at the early morning sky which I now stop and admire more these days. And then I thought, good thing I don't have my camera so that I can just drink in this moment, instead of worrying about capturing the perfect picture. My boyfriend is in the midst of a major flare up of gout, which he has experienced from time to time. In my quest to express my concern and empathy I offered several suggestions. Much later in the conversation, he revealed that he thought I wasn't empathetic and came across as blaming him for being in this situation. Even though it's difficult for me to realize that I'm not showing up with empathy and concern I appreciate that he is willing to give me the feedback so I can make adjustments in the future. Change isn't easy, but I never want to make someone I love feel judged or blamed for the things they have little control over.

I am a proud Gramma of 10 grandkiddos. The youngest one has been staying with us 3 days and 2 nights/week since daycare closed a year ago. A friend down south of us about 30 miles raises strawberries and they were maturing and ripe for the picking. I contacted her to see if I could bring my 2 year old grandson to "pick" strawberries. She welcomed us. She patiently showed him how to pick the berries and he picked up on that endeavor pretty good, scurrying from bush to bush. I then showed him that he could eat the berries (he had never had that experience). It wasn't long and he was "pickin' & eatin' - two fisted no less! He was in the height of glory. The next day we made freezer strawberry jam and he was "helping" me. If I hadn't had his help I think I would have gotten 9 jars instead of 7!!

This was a simple thing to do. It rained yesterday pretty hard. Where I live, we do not get much rain so I decided I would use the opportunity to wash the car using the rain water. It wasn't to cold and I finished fairly quickly. The car turned out well, even though there was still water drops on the car, they were not dirty ones that leave muddy marks on the vehicle. It was fun and weird at the same time, but it was nice to do something different.

yesterday I was walking my dogs I have 2 around the sports fields after just getting one of them groomed. There was rain yesterday and it was soaked everywhere I let my dogs run and was just walking in the rain enjoying the outdoors because of covid 19 I don't have a great deal of outdoor time. I looked up to make sure there were no other dogs coming as my one dog is not very friendly, I could see the one dog but the other one was no where to be seen I started calling her but nothing. For dinner last night we had a perennial pandemic favorite, and I'm almost embarrassed to admit what it was. We had grilled cheese sandwiches and tomato soup - a meal perhaps more suitable for a nine year old. But it's delicious and quick and everyone enjoys it. In fact, I even bought a cast iron griddle to accommodate more simultaneous sandwich grilling. This strange, unprecedented time creates all sorts of stresses and challenges, so when we find something that brings a small measure of comfort, we grab it. Last night's dinner was one of those things.

My day yesterday was a quiet and boring day to some but it was great to me to just be alive. My sister passed away a few weeks ago so I know it can happen very suddenly when it's your turn to go. My day was spent mostly outside at the patio. I had my coffee outside sitting in the rocking chair watching the birds. I have two little finch birds that come down to me and they sit on the patio wall and just chirp away. I really wonder what they are saying to me. I check out and water my roses that my daughter and her husband brought to me a few weeks ago. One is deep red and the other is a beautiful pink, though the pink one is growing better than the red, with a lot of bloom. After supper I went on the computer till ten, and then I read the Bible for half a hour, then I crocheted. I make chemo hats and mail them to a cancer center where she splits them up and then sends them out to different chemo sites. I enjoy crocheting and figure this is the best I can do to help other people. Then I went to bed at eleven thirty.

At the beginning of this year I lost my dream house to foreclosure. Yesterday I received a dunning letter for that property demand annual dues fore this year. I am conflicted as to whether I should ignore them or write them a stern letter imploring them to get their act together.
I went to another town to see a specialist about back surgery. I found out that it would entail placing rods and screws in my back. I choose to never have this done unless I am paralyzed.

Yesterday I got up at 5 AM like I normally do. I meditated and ate breakfast. My knee felt a little gimpy so instead of going for a run I decided to walk to the grocery store. There an back is almost five miles. I left home around 6:30. It was a beautiful morning and I was enjoying the walk a great deal. Before I went inside the store I put on my mask. I selected a couple of russet potatoes, a Vidalia onion, a pint of blueberries, and a container of Brummel & Brown butter-like spread. It's low-cal and made with yogurt according to the label. I was at Food Lion which doesn't have self-checkout, so I waited in line behind a group of firefighters who were stocking up for the station apparently. I was really amazed that the five of them were standing in a group and not one of them was wearing a mask. I was tempted to take a picture and post it on Facebook. First-responders should set an example instead of giving conspiracy-theorist morons a reason not to comply with CDC recommendations. Not wanting to get anyone in trouble, I didn't take the picture. I paid for my purchase and enjoyed my walk home. I settled in to work at my home office about 8:30. Almost my whole workday was spent reading journals and reviewing data. No emails, no messages, no Skype or Teams. I actually got some work done. After dinner I watched a movie and read for a bit. I ended my day by meditating, as I usually do. I went to bed around 10 PM.

I knew something was wrong from the moment I sat down behind the wheel. The smell just wasn't right. I had been noticing it for several weeks, but I just assumed it was typical Florida mustiness associated with summertime. When I dropped my phone on the floor, I had no idea of the shock I was about to receive. When I picked up the phone, my hand grazed against the carpeting alongside the floor mat. It came back wet. Confused, I pressed my finger into the carpeting. It was soaking wet. As a matter of fact, the ENTIRE floor of my Yaris was soaking wet. That explained the musty smell I'd been noticing. But what to do about it? Fast forward 24 hours and one trip to the local Toyota dealership--a trip I'd rather not have made. When the verdict came back, it was even worse news than I'd expected. My 11-year-old Yaris had finally begun to show its age. A rotting windshield gasket had been allowing water to seep into the car, unbeknownst to me. So here I am, sitting at home on a Friday night, no car and about to be $2000 lighter in the wallet when the repairs are completed. Oh well, my friends told me to think twice about canceling the comprehensive coverage on my car insurance.

The virus is rising again, winter is coming, outdoor activities are going to be less possible. We talked about the possibility of taking a few days and going to the coast, taking a room with a kitchen and cooking our own meals. We love walking on the beach, enjoying the crashing surf. But it is cold. 478 new cases in Oregon today, 82 in Lane County, we can't run the risk of infection by going out to eat. "What do you want to do?" he asked. "I want to go, but do I want to go and not be able to visit the shops we love, eat in the restaurants we love, just stay in a hotel room and cook our meals?" I thought about it. I guess I am getting cabin fever. It has been nearly 9 months since my doc told me, "Stay Home!" and I have except for a few doc appointments, dropping by the pharmacy on the way home for the new drugs. I have risked eating take out from our favorite restaurants, and survived. "You know, I think we should wait. I don't feel particularly well today, coughing, nearly constantly, it would be terrible to be away from home and get the virus."

I have a friend that I have known for many years, since we went to college together. He lives in another part of the same state that I live in. We e-mail each other every day, sometimes with serious news, but mostly with humorous stories, jokes, etc., which has been great for my mood during the coronavirus crisis. A few years ago, I drove down to where he lives and met his wife and two children, a little boy and a little girl. They both seemed normal to me at the time, and I thought that any problems my friend was having with them were the same as other families. Yesterday, in an e-mail, I asked my friend how the little girl is doing, and my friend said it's been very difficult, because she is autistic. I asked if more than one doctor has confirmed that, and my friend said yes, and that his son is also autistic, but he functions better than his daughter. I was really surprised, and felt bad for my friend, thinking about how difficult it must be to have two autistic children.

Yesterday included a drive in church service. We all stayed distant and in our cars while listening to the singing. Pastor had a great message for us. All of this was displayed on a high up platform outside. We were able to listen clearly as we tuned in on our FM radios. Parking lot had to be extended to contain the crowd. While being socially distant is not the same as being in a building together, it was fun waiving to the people on the right and the left. Following that enjoyed sitting with spouse and just appreciating the time of chatting and being together. Afternoon and evening was spent relaxing, talking with friends on social media, and catching up on the news.

Yesterday was a fascinating day, to say the least. Despite a beautiful late-spring day in the making, it started to look like a really bleak one, indeed. Our pets both got sick, the neighbors were starting to be annoyingly noisy, my computer was acting up - making me restart it at least a half-dozen times - and even though we wanted to go pick up lunch at a drive-up, all the available drive-ups in the area were way too busy for us to get in a line and wait. So, we came back home, fixed a couple of really boring sandwiches, and made the best of it. Early evening, we watched the national news, as we always do, just to learn that our government was doing even more unpalatable things about this pandemic, while our state government was behaving exactly opposite - doing all the smart things, making us feel deeply grateful for living where we do. Our pets were finally feeling better, so we spent part of the evening playing with them, and the rest watching a special movie we'd been wanting to see for some time. So, a day that started off very badly ended up being a very pleasant one instead. Fascinating, indeed!

We accomplished what we were there for. My sister dropped me off back at home. She went on with her day and I did as well.

Yesterday was a day where I spent most of it looking for work on Mturk and cleaning. Yesterday I spent the day sheltering in place due to Covid 19, having a day very similar to every other day for the past six weeks or so. My day started with opening my eyes to a brand new day, heating up a cup of decaf, feeding the dog, letting him outside, then turning on the computer. The next thing I did was turn on the television to see if there were any changes since yesterday in the news. People all over the world are doing their best to survive this horrible illness. I am so sorry for those who have succumbed, and those healthcare workers who are trying so hard to help people survive. After catching up on the news, off goes the television. Next I let the dog back in, and get on MTurk and see if there is any work for me. I don't use scripts, I look for the individual studies that are interesting, and legitimate. I am doing my best to keep my mind healthy during this time of isolation. I am in the high risk category with covid so I have to stay away from other humans. I look forward to participating in the studies, and hope that my answers help the studies. I get to feel like I can contribute something when I participate. After a period of working, I cleaned my house, exercised in my living room, then prepared my soup and salad for the day. Yesterday I made salad with Italian salad greens, avocado, and red onion and tomato. My soup was made in the crock pot, with beans, corn, pasta, and tomato sauce with spices. Yesterday evening I had vegan burger and potato. Snack was bean chips. During the day I went back to Mturk between cooking and meals and cleaning. At night I watched television. I also texted with family and a friend yesterday. We are staying in contact with each other and keeping each other engaged and aware of current events and helping each other stay positive.

Just yesterday, I found out that my mother's sister died. I had not seen her in years, but so many nostalgic memories came flooding back. My aunt had 16 children and lived in a 2-room house. Some might have even called it a shack. However, the house was always spotless and my aunt was a very hard worker. I'm not sure I ever saw more than a handful of my cousins at one time. I don't think I ever even met all 16 of them. My aunt and her husband raised a large garden. Her house was way out in the country and it seemed to take forever to get there. What I remember vividly is the taste of her pickled corn. It was the best I've ever had.

I spent considerable time deep cleaning my guest bathroom. I had a guest over during this covid time and they used the bathroom. I keep a meticulous house at all times. I do not allow anyone into my home since this virus forced everyone into a lock down lifestyle. I am definitely on the high risk category so I felt almost violated by someone using my bathroom. Immediately after the guest left, I donned plastic gloves and disinfectant cleaner and scoured the entire bathroom including washing walls and floors. Even after the deep cleaning, I still feel it is not clean enough. I never was a true germaphobic but now I must reassess my opinions.

In the time of Covid-19, personal life events of any significance are rarer than usual! However, luckily for this survey, something of at least slight note did happen yesterday. I am a writer, and I participated in an online interview/book chat with another author about one of my series. The interview used a video streaming app that I hadn't used before, but worked well and easily. When the video stream started, my image was ridiculously close-up on the screen, so I had to wheel my chair further back from my computer than I would normally sit, but that did seem to fix the problem. It was a little awkward, but we managed. I also found that my glasses reflected badly in the video, which is not usually a problem with my webcam, but there was nothing I could do about that. The chat went well, although I wished the interviewer had sent me the questions in advance so that I could have been more prepared. She asked me one question about one of my main character's likes and dislikes, and for a moment I drew a horrible blank! But the video was live, so I had to scramble to think of something to say. All in all I think the interview went well, although of course after it was over, I thought of much better answers I could have given. That's always the way. :) It's why I'm a writer instead of a speaker. I think better with my fingers.

Yesterday, while observing our stay at home order. I helped my husband defrost the freezer. I threw out a trash bag full of different types of bread I had made over the last few years and meant to use, but it got out of hand. Yesterday was day 35 of working alone in my office. Everyone else is working from home because of the COVID-19 shelter in place order. The office is closed to the public, but every day I have come in at 8 a.m., disarmed the alarm, turned on the lights, and started my work day. I've collected the mail, answered the dispatch radio, and done my solitary work quietly. I have been deemed essential and I am thankful to have a job, but I am lonely. I miss my co-workers and the hustle and bustle of everyone in the office. I even miss the phone ringing and waiting on customers. I sometimes feel as if I am in a post-apocalytic universe and it creeps me out a little. I ate my lunch quietly and just keep doing my work. Sometimes for a break I popped on to a couple of news sites on the web and read about pandemic news. It's actually a good thing I was by myself because I found myself crying a little bit. Crying for all of the people suffering and for those who have died. Crying because I am by myself. Crying because life is different and it won't go back to being anything close to normal for a very long time. Crying because I am selfish for missing my "normal" life when others have lost family and friends and will never get back to a normal life. I kept going, though, and finished my work day again. Shut off the computer, turned off the lights, and set the alarm. I went straight back home, ate dinner, and went to bed.....upset that I knew I'd have to do the same thing for many more days.

Yesterday was much the same as the day before. We are still practicing social distancing and wearing masks to ward off the coronavirus. My husband and I are together and after fifty plus years of marriage are still meeting challenges. He has dementia and things are really different now. I spend my days taking care of his needs as well as a bit of time on my computer to keep me connected to the world outside. I prepared his breakfast and make sure he washes his hands. Its important with the virus so omnipresent. I ordered groceries online to avoid mixing with anyone who might be infected. I cannot take chances considering my age and my husband's health. It is a precarious situation and we are doing our best to stay healthy. I tend to his needs as well as those of my five cats who are a joyous part of our household. Its like having five little beings that are comedians. I read for a bit a book by Lee Child called Blue Moon. I have read the entire series and enjoy the escapism. Soon I prepare lunch and then my husband goes down for a nap and I do a tv watching on a streaming station. I pay bills online and prepare dinner. We take a walk outside and enjoy the garden. I love flowers and work in my yard daily. Although my life is different, I can always find some joy whether in the antics of my cats or the beauty in my garden.

Yesterday I had my third night in a row experience with insomnia. For some reason I could just not sleep through the night. I had always thought insomnia should be something easy to rectify - that as long as you were not too busy or self absorbed you would surely be able to fall asleep. Until then I had figured it was just a passing thing the two nights before and not a real issue. Yesterday However nothing worked again. No hot showers , no drink consumed , no technique I had used before with limited success. I just couldn't fall asleep even when I lied down for an hour with my eyes closed. I eventually gave up and did some remote work and watched a movie. I then had an early breakfast and went through the day in a haze until nodding off at my desk for an hour or two. During the pandemic I work 100% from home so the impact of this new experience has had less impact on my work life than it normally would . Its easier to work through the day tired if there's no commute and getting ready for work but my search online and of has begun because insomnia can be as debilitating as a major illness.

Yesterday I learned how to change a mirror on the driver side of my car. I live in a City now and the driver side mirror was broken off. It was expensive to fix when I got a dealer estimate. This is a small life event, but made my day. My neighbor and I often complain about the parking outside. One week my can was so full I barely wheeled it to the curb and there it was minutes before the truck came in the middle of the sidewalk. Then, there was yesterday. I was putting out the sprinklers and got a surprise shower while switching from sprayer to sprinkler. As I was grumbling, a young Muslim woman and her son walked across the street. I had never seen them before, so went back to my hose. But, she wanted my attention. So, I stopped what I was doing to see what she needed. As she went on her way, I had a smile on my face. It does not take much to be considerate and respectful. It doesn't take much to let another person know that you are neighborly. It is annoying to feel you are being taken advantage of. I appreciated her asking in advance.

It has been difficult having a social life in the midst of a pandemic. With most businesses closed and social distancing still a requirement finding human contact is tricky. My neighbor in my building has arranged what she calls hallway coffee. She organized a time for us all to bring chairs into the hallway along with coffee and we would sit together and catch up. Yesterday we met just after lunch. Everyone six feet apart but together in the same space. The coffee date lasted almost an hour as we swapped anecdotes about shopping and trying to follow directional arrows in grocery stores, what have become our favorite walks around the neighborhood and how well we think the shut down measures have been in tamping down the number of infections. We all agreed that we will be happy when we can abandon the new normal for some better semblance of the old.

Not for everyone, but for very many of us, growing older means watching our lives grow smaller. The triumphs and defeats--the drama--of our youths are behind us and we are well-advised to learn to be content with the smaller stage that we now occupy. I am reminded of this circumstance almost every day. Yesterday, for example, I turned on the drip system to the plants in my backyard, limped across the front lawn to water a shrub that is struggling and used the water wand to irrigate the hanging baskets of flowers on my front porch. Running down the mental list of garden maintenance still undone, I settled on cutting back some vines. The honeysuckle overruns the fence into the neighbor's yard and the wild roses stubbornly insist on sprawling far beyond the limits of the flower bed. So, I clipped and trimmed for about fifteen minutes--that's as long as I can stay on my feet without a rest--and gathered up the clippings in a plastic yard waste bag. Just before I went back inside, I grabbed up three or four branches from the rose bushes. I put them in a tall glass vase on my desk. The wild roses are not so sophisticated as their cultivated cousins, but the red is vivid, real.

I used to like squirrels. I always thought they looked like they were having a great time; jumping from limb to limb and virtually flying through the air like some sort of little furry, bushy tailed, trapeze artist. It always made me happy to watch them. But lately, yesterday included, a particular squirrel is beginning to test my patience. Every morning, I fill a bird feeder and hang it in the tree outside my kitchen window. This feeder has become quite the breakfast hot spot for most of the neighborhood birds; there is often a wait, and the spillover crowd fills the branches surrounding the feeder. All this activity has attracted the attention of an inquisitive squirrel, who has found that he can jump into the tree, run along the branch and pull the top off of the bird feeder, spilling all the food onto the ground below. He then jumps down and feasts on his sunflower seed booty. I have caught him in the act a couple of times; usually a sharp rap on the kitchen window makes him scurry away; but not yesterday. Yesterday, he defied me. He ignored my kitchen window warning and continued to try and upend the feeder, knowing all the while that I was watching him. He actually stared at me through the kitchen window, eyes full of defiance, forcing me to open the back door and walk towards the tree before he ran up high, barking and chattering his complaints the whole way. For a brief moment, his particular squirrel's aggressive and disruptive behavior made me wary of all squirrels, or at least it did for a couple of minutes, I think I'm over it now.

My father passed away less than a week ago. He was almost 88 years old and in fairly reasonable physical health. He went into medical distress and did not recover. I was honoured by my family to write my father’s obituary. Due to Covid-19 restrictions, we could not cross the border into a neighbouring province. We missed the viewing that was held three days ago but hope we will be able to attend the memorial and burial service this spring, all together as a family. I know the grieving process now has really just begun as reality sets in. That is the context and background of my story. Yesterday, I took a couple of hours by myself and for myself. Yesterday was like every other day. After catching up on the news, with once again the monster Trump dominating life in America, I spent the day completing tasks on Mechanical Turk. Having lost all of my assets, including retirement funds, due to health issues some years ago, I survive on a monthly Social Security check of US$1,256. The relatively small earnings from MTurk help me get through the month. Yesterday was the first day of the month; the third day of each month is when my Social Security check arrives by direct deposit into my bank account. These last several days of the month, I am once again completely out of money. I have to get through two more days, until the third, when I will have funds again. Yesterday and today I will feed myself and Summer on whatever I can scrounge from the kitchen. I may have just enough pocket change for an outdated loaf of bread at the supermarket and two cans of reasonably good cat food. I wish I had something to look forward to. I wish I had a best friend to talk to. I wish Katherine, another cat who succumbed to cancer two months ago, could come back. She always brought a smile to my face and a reason to face each day.
